evidence.mission_note: It fits the enthusiast-bridge brief directly: a naturally aspirated manual with simple Toyota/Subaru mechanicals in California that should resell easily within 6-24 months. Its price sits above the ideal band but under the ceiling, and it is a secondary candidate to the Z3 3.0i.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN is stated, the decode matches a 2018 BRZ 2.0L coupe, the price is itemised at $22,017 including fees, and the one photo of this car shows a stock-looking Ice Silver Limited with Performance Package Brembo calipers. Ownership (single owner) and accident history (none reported) come only from Autotrader's summary; the report itself is not attached, and a clean report means no reported event. Nothing is observed wrong. The only listing inconsistencies are minor equipment-list conflicts on upholstery and wheels. What remains open is the maintenance half of the evidence: no service records, no proof that recall 21V587000 (fuel pump), which applies to this VIN, was done, no tire dates, and no disclosure on track use or tune status. At $21,895 the car sits above the $19,815 fair-value midpoint, near the top of the comp range, which low mileage and the Performance Package partly explain.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer for the full Carfax, a Subaru recall printout for 21V587000, tire DOT codes and service records, and confirm they will allow an independent PPI in Anaheim before any deposit.
